hero.title: The Indo-Greeks: Pioneers of Hellenistic Influence
hero.description: An analytical study of the Yavana kingdoms in post-Mauryan India, highlighting their cultural synthesis and numismatic legacy.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Key milestones marking the transition of the Greco-Bactrian rule into the Indo-Greek kingdoms.

cards.details: Demetrius I crosses the Hindu Kush, initiating the invasion of northwestern India.
Reign of Menander I (Milinda), the most prominent Indo-Greek ruler, reaching the zenith of their power.
Final dissolution of the Indo-Greek kingdoms under the pressure of Scythian (Saka) invasions.

items.title: D.M.A
items.decryption: The 'Big Three' Indo-Greeks: Demetrius (The Pioneer), Menander (The Scholar-King), and Apollodotus (The Expander).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Do not confuse Indo-Greeks with the Indo-Scythians (Sakas); Indo-Greeks minted the first gold coins in India, not the Kushans.
Menander was not an immediate convert to Buddhism; the 'Milinda Panha' records a dialogue leading to his intellectual leaning, not necessarily total conversion.
The Gandhara School of Art is a result of fusion, not purely Greek.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Bactria (North of Hindu Kush).
  • Extended to Punjab, Indus Valley, and parts of Gangetic plain.
  • Capital: Sakala (Modern Sialkot).

Personalities

  • Demetrius I: First to invade.
  • Menander: Famous 'Milinda Panha' figure.
  • Heliodorus: Envoy at Besnagar.

Cultural Synthesis Mindmap

  • Numismatics: Introduction of bilingual/biscriptal coins (Greek + Kharosthi). First to issue gold coins in India.
  • Art & Architecture: Evolution of Gandhara School of Art (Buddha in Hellenistic style).
  • Religious Impact: Patronage of Buddhism; assimilation into local society (Yavanas).
